rationale.text: Map each row (i) to a distinct thread block (threadblock.x). LayerNorm is embarrassingly parallel across rows — each row is independent. With M=64 rows and 30 SMs, this gives ~2 waves of 32 blocks each, saturating the GPU. This is the canonical high-performance layernorm pattern: one CTA per row handles the full reduction over N=2048.

Vectorize the inner j-loop with width 4 (float4 / 128-bit loads). N=2048 is divisible by 4, enabling coalesced 128-bit memory transactions. This reduces the number of memory instructions by 4×, maximizing memory bandwidth utilization on Ampere's L2/HBM. Width-4 is the sweet spot for FP32 (4×4B = 16B = 128-bit, matching cache line granularity).
